title: Software engineering assessment series under human-machine teaching strategies
summary: Students complete ten classroom tests, ten homework tasks, and a final exam after directive, guided-AI, or student-led GenAI-supported instruction. AI is used during guided and collaborative learning, while the assessment series measures immediate knowledge, independent exploration, and integrated problem solving.

sources.title: Research on the Effectiveness of Human-Machine Collaborative Teaching Based on Data Analysis in the Era of Digital Intelligence
sources.evidence_quote: Classroom tests consisted primarily of objective questions

assessment.summary: Complete classroom tests, homework, and a comprehensive final exam in software engineering.
student_actions: Explore and solve subjective homework tasks.
Integrate course concepts in a final exam.

outputs.artifact: Test answers, homework responses, and final-exam responses

student_role.description: GenAI supported learning in two treatment groups; the source does not state AI availability during tests or the final exam.

grading.method: Online objective tests, instructor-graded homework, and mixed automated/human final-exam grading.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

reported_results: Quasi-experiment with 99 students across three intact classes.
